expectations.text: The check command exits 0 (no files created or changed)
The reply identifies path traversal via the file parameter (e.g. ../ or an absolute path makes os.path.join escape UPLOADS)
expectations.evidence: The reply says "`?file=../../../etc/passwd` becomes `/srv/app/uploads/../../../etc/passwd`, which resolves to `/etc/passwd`" and "if `name` is absolute, `os.path.join` throws away `UPLOADS` entirely."

expectations.text: The reply names that any logged-in user can read files outside uploads, including other users' files, as the affected boundary
expectations.evidence: The reply says "anyone can read any file the app process has permission to read" and "anyone (or any logged-in user) can download every other user's uploads". That covers both files outside uploads and other users' files, with an attacker group that includes any logged-in user.
